findings.evidence: be/scripts/db-backup.ts writes VACUUM INTO straight to the final path (line 26) and only verifies afterwards (lines 35-37). Nothing removes the output when the run is interrupted or fails: the catch (lines 28-32) calls fail() without rmSync(out). Reproduced on a 253 MB copy of the seeded DB: `db-backup.ts $S/bk_out.db` killed with SIGKILL at ~350 ms left a 127-145 MB bk_out.db plus a 1024-byte bk_out.db-journal at the FINAL name. (1) A re-run to the same target answers `Refusing to overwrite ...` exit 2, as if a good backup existed. (2) `db:check` on it prints a raw stack trace (`attempt to write a readonly database`, errcode 776), no verdict. (3) Copying bk_out.db WITH its -journal and starting the API on it boots silently: GET /api/health 200, `select count(*) from users` = 0, user_version 7 (the hot journal rolls the file back to an empty database and the server migrates it as a fresh DB). Copying bk_out.db alone gives `cannot start: file is not a database`. Same leftover on SIGINT/SIGTERM (default handlers, no cleanup) and on disk-full (generic catch). Line 31 also reports a genuine 'locked/busy' VACUUM failure as 'Refusing to overwrite' whenever the partial file exists. No finding in the live-DB path: VACUUM INTO taken every ~2.4 s during a 45 s chaos run with 10 SIGKILLs produced 7 snapshots that all passed the full invariant suite.
findings.fix_hint: VACUUM INTO `${out}.partial`, verify integrity, chmod, then rename to `out` (atomic); on any failure or SIGINT/SIGTERM rmSync the partial and its -journal; keep the 'Refusing to overwrite' message only for an existing final file.

findings.category: multi-process write contention / availability (challenges R13-A-06 as documented)
findings.evidence: KNOWN_LIMITATIONS R13-A-06 says only that 'requests that need the lock answer 500 after 5-10 s'. Two facts it omits, both reproduced: (a) GET read endpoints need the write lock: Game.badges() (game.ts:269) runs tx(BEGIN IMMEDIATE) on every call and is reached from GET /api/dashboard (game.ts:651), GET /api/profile (game.ts:738) and GET /api/badges. (b) node:sqlite busy-waits synchronously, so the whole event loop is blocked, not just the request. Repro: second connection runs BEGIN IMMEDIATE on the DB file; as a student, concurrently GET /api/health, /api/me, /api/dashboard, /api/badges, /api/leaderboard, /api/profile, /api/labs. Result: health 200 in 5 ms (before the first lock wait), dashboard 500 at 5499 ms, badges 500 at 10964 ms, profile 500 at 16443 ms, and a GET /api/health sent at t=300 ms was answered only at 16448 ms (a liveness probe would fail and restart the pod). Also reproduced the paid-hint variant: with a 2 s assistant call, lock taken by another connection right after the charge commit -> POST /hint answers `500 internal_error` after 7.5 s while the attempt shows hintsUsed 1, penaltyXp -15 and hintsGiven [standard text]; the learner is charged and gets an error body (a retry buys level 2 for another -15). Needs a second writer that holds the lock > 5 s (second API process running a long reset, manual sqlite session), so multi-process only.
findings.fix_hint: Make GET paths read-only (move the badge catch-up to the write paths or a one-time migration; HEAD already skips it), answer 503 + Retry-After on SQLITE_BUSY, and keep health independent of the DB (or SELECT 1 only). Optionally return the stored standard hint in the 500 path of /hint tx2.

findings.category: audit chain integrity (defence in depth, not API reachable)
findings.evidence: content_audit 'append-only' is enforced by BEFORE UPDATE / BEFORE DELETE triggers only (db.ts migrations 4 and 5). `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO content_audit (id, ..., actor_name) VALUES (1, ..., 'FORGED')` on a migrated DB succeeded and `select actor_name from content_audit where id=1` returned 'FORGED': REPLACE deletes the conflicting row without firing DELETE triggers because recursive_triggers is OFF (not set anywhere in db.ts). UPDATE and DELETE were correctly refused. Also a teacher user row can be deleted without touching audit rows (by design, no FK). No HTTP route can reach this (31 routes enumerated, no SQL surface; 16 concurrent reviewers x 2 missions x 30 racing transitions across 2 processes left an unbroken from/to chain equal to content_status), so only someone with file access can forge a row.
findings.fix_hint: PRAGMA recursive_triggers = ON in openDb (or a BEFORE INSERT trigger that aborts when NEW.id already exists); optionally store a hash of the previous row for a verifiable chain.

findings.evidence: Game.competencies() (game.ts:575-582) takes the latest solved result per step from ANY attempt, including in-progress and expired ones that were never completed. Repro as a fresh student: complete hem-01 and hem-02 with no mistakes -> GET /api/competencies Pre-analytical quality 100%. Start a replay of hem-02, answer step 1 wrong x3 then correct, leave the attempt open -> Pre-analytical quality 67% while profile xp.total stays 360 and accuracyPct 100. The drop appears before the replay is finished (or if it expires) and is shown in result payloads and strongest/improvement advice. The doc lists 'latest attempt per step' but not that unfinished attempts count.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict competencies() to step_results of attempts with status = 'completed' (join attempts a ... AND a.status = 'completed').

findings.evidence: docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md line 40 (Technical limits) still says that stopping the server while an AI hint is generated 'keeps the hint penalty without delivering the text ... such a hint is counted but has no stored text, so it never appears in the list of earlier hints'. Round 16 (R16-A-02) made the charge and the standard text one commit. Verified: SIGKILL 500 ms into a 1.5 s assistant call, restart -> hint_log row (level 1, source 'standard', text 'Ignore the round cells with central pallor.') and hints_total 1; the attempt lists it in step.hintsGiven. The stale sentence is not marked superseded (unlike R10-A-10).
findings.fix_hint: Rewrite or delete the line; point to R16-A-02.
